prompt: Original educational conceptual illustration, landscape 3:2. Warm ivory paper, sophisticated hand-painted gouache/watercolour, confident fine brown outlines, navy lettering, restrained teal, coral and amber. Editorial science illustration with spacious composition and large legible labels. The explanatory structure must carry the meaning visually: molecules, objects, geometry or flow; never paragraphs in boxes. No organs, regional anatomy, teeth or joint cutaways, tissue layers, invented histology, diagnostic photographs, radiographs or patient data. All symbols are explicitly conceptual. Footer: 'Conceptual teaching model • Not to scale'. Title 'Dome + central dimple', subtitle 'Shape vocabulary for molluscum'. Use pure sculpture geometry: two large warm cream clay domes sitting on separate wooden plinths against ivory paper. Left dome smooth convex hemisphere, labelled 'Dome'. Right dome equally sized but with a SMALL SHALLOW CENTRAL DEPRESSION, labelled 'Central dimple', a fine leader precisely ending in the depression. This is not a hole through the dome and not a crater destroying the dome. Under the right sculpture, draw a single navy exterior profile line: convex upward left shoulder, tiny down-dip at centre, convex right shoulder; label 'Umbilication'. This line is silhouette only with empty white space beneath, no layers or cutaway. Bottom text 'Clay model, not a diagnostic skin image'. No skin texture, body, pus, pores or clinical lesion.

teaching.question: What does central umbilication mean when describing a molluscum papule?
teaching.answer: It means a small central depression in an otherwise dome-shaped papule. This is a characteristic shape description, not a diagnosis by itself.

title: Dome plus central dimple
caption: A typical molluscum papule has a dome-like contour with central umbilication. This clay model teaches the shape term and is not a diagnostic skin image.
alt: A clay dome is compared with an otherwise similar dome containing a shallow central dimple; top and side silhouettes clarify the contour.

review.notes: Paired clay hemispheres differ by a small central depression on the right; leader terminates in the shallow dimple. Exterior profile line reproduces the central dip without layers or internal contents. Text explicitly calls this a clay shape model, not a diagnostic skin image. No clinical lesion simulation.
